faq.question: After Class 12, are Indian students able to pursue computer engineering studies in Canada?
faq.answer: Indeed. If they fulfill the academic, math, physics, and other subject requirements of the university, Indian students can apply to **undergraduate computer engineering programs in Canada after Class 12**.

faq.question: Is JEE a prerequisite for admission to computer engineering programs in Canada?
faq.answer: JEE is typically not a prerequisite for admission to Canadian colleges. Academic achievement in Class 12 and university-specific requirements are typically used to determine admission. Students should constantly review the prerequisites of the universities they have selected.

faq.question: How long does computer engineering take in Canada?
faq.answer: It typically takes four years to complete an undergraduate degree in computer engineering. Options like co-ops or internships could increase the overall time.

faq.question: How much does it cost Indian students to study computer engineering in Canada?
faq.answer: As a general planning estimate, living expenditures and tuition might come to at least CAD 52,400-115,400 annually. The actual costs differ depending on the program, city, and university. Q 5. After earning my computer engineering degree, can I get employment in Canada? Graduates can work in computing, electronics, embedded systems, hardware development, telecommunications, and related fields. The student's circumstances, employer needs, and the immigration laws in force at the time of application all affect their eligibility for employment and post-graduation work permits. A Canadian degree does not ensure employment, a work permit, or long-term residency. Q 6. Which Canadian institutions provide the top computer engineering programs? The University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, University of British Columbia, McGill University, University of Alberta, McMaster University, and Carleton University are among the universities that offer computer engineering or programs closely linked to it. Before making a decision, students should examine program specifics, entrance requirements, tuition costs, and accreditation.
